A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Revela and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Inspection of all 20 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2 supports a reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Revela experiments on BEIR and CoIR, alongside training configuration and architectural ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original retrieval experiments on CoIR, BRIGHT, and BEIR, plus controlled comparisons, generalization experiments, and evaluation of the co-trained LM.

M1.justification: The joint next-token prediction objective, retriever-weighted in-batch attention, and embedding procedure remain. However, V-normalization, presented as a general component in v1 Section 3.2, becomes specific to Wikipedia training; v2 Appendix B.5 explicitly uses unnormalized attention for code training. The optional Revela+BM25 reciprocal-rank-fusion variant is also removed.

E1.justification: v2 adds BRIGHT's reasoning-intensive retrieval tasks, Fineweb-edu training with cross-domain evaluation, and seven LM capability benchmarks. It also evaluates Wikipedia-trained retrievers on CoIR and code-trained retrievers on BEIR. The original Wikipedia and code training sources remain, but v1's experiment incorporating five BEIR corpora into training disappears.

E2.justification: v2 adds E5-PT to the retrieval comparisons, BGE-M3 and E5-Mistral to CoIR, and E5-Mistral plus additional API embedding models to BRIGHT. RetroMAE and RepLLaMA disappear from the BEIR comparison, while GraphCodeBERT and the original Contriever baseline disappear from the main CoIR comparison. Retained citations or checkpoint listings do not preserve those evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Retriever configurations expand from 135M–1B to include 3B models and an 8B BRIGHT model, with smaller batches for the larger models. The batch-size sweep changes from 8/12/16 to 4/8/16. New protocols include the controlled LLaMA-3.2-1B Contriever experiment, specifying 15 negatives per query and an effective batch size of 256, and accuracy-based evaluation of LM capability retention.

E4.justification: v2 adds a training-dynamics case study, a comparison controlling the Contriever backbone, cross-domain transfer analyses, Fineweb-edu robustness experiments, and an LM capability-retention analysis. Conversely, v1's random-batch construction, LoRA-rank, V-normalization, and BEIR-corpus augmentation analyses are removed. LM-size and mixed-domain studies survive with revised results, while the batch-size analysis uses a revised sweep.

E5.justification: v1 Section 4.2 reports a z-test with p < 10^-9 for the retrieval improvements. v2 removes this significance-test reporting and supplies no replacement test, repeated-run counts, seed information, or uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: Numerous retained results change: the reported 1B BEIR means move from 42.3 to 42.7 for Revela and from 35.2 to 35.7 for REPLUG. Revela's 1B CoIR mean changes from 54.6 to 58.6 alongside the normalization change, so this is not an unchanged-procedure gain. New results include 60.1 for Revela-3B on CoIR and 17.8 for Revela-8B on BRIGHT, plus controlled, transfer, and LM-retention results. Removed analyses also lose their result entries.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix C.7 adds a computational-cost argument contrasting B^2(2L)^2 for REPLUG with B(2L)^2 for Revela, assuming backward cost approximately equals forward cost. This is a new analytical claim, without a formal theorem or proof. The retained Wikipedia V-normalization equations are relocated rather than newly derived.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes improvements over REPLUG on BEIR and CoIR. v2 expands the central claims to surpassing larger supervised retrievers and proprietary APIs on CoIR, matching strong models on BRIGHT, and achieving BEIR state-of-the-art parity with approximately 1000 times less training data and 10 times less compute. Stronger cross-domain generalization than contrastive learning also becomes an explicit contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the controlled comparisons as evidence of stronger cross-domain generalization and attributes LM capability preservation plausibly to LoRA and the retained NTP objective. It qualifies V-normalization as beneficial for Wikipedia but unfavorable for code and introduces possible multimodal applicability. Conversely, v1's substantive limitations concerning multilingual coverage and dependence on document structure disappear, as does its discussion of catastrophic degradation under random batch construction.

D1.justification: Most original training hyperparameters, hardware specifications, and REPLUG replication details remain. v2 adds training times of approximately 44/48 hours, a 2048-token inference limit, NLTK chunking, the Wikipedia document count, controlled-Contriever implementation details, additional checkpoint identifiers, and a 3B weights link replacing the 1B link. The RRF recipe and explicit token-budget equalization statement for batch-size experiments disappear. Newly disclosed settings do not establish changes to earlier execution.

R1.justification: The research positioning shifts substantially toward comparison with E5's large-scale weakly supervised pair construction and strong supervised/API retrievers, emphasizing avoidance of pair curation and resource efficiency. References supporting E5, BGE-M3, BRIGHT, Fineweb, LM evaluation, and multimodal retrieval are added. Discussion and citations for Co-Condenser, Condenser, TSDAE, and Doc2Query are removed or condensed away.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, results narrative, and analysis organization are substantially rewritten. CoIR becomes the leading evaluation, analysis topics are reordered, and substantial material moves into reorganized appendices. Discussion becomes Future Directions, and new reproducibility and LLM-use statements appear. Citation style changes from numbered references to author–year.

P2.justification: v2 restructures the CoIR comparison table, relocates the detailed BEIR comparison to the appendix, and introduces a combined BRIGHT/BEIR summary figure. It adds training-dynamics heatmaps and several new analysis tables while removing the normalization and BEIR-augmentation figures. Retained scaling plots are redrawn with revised panel ordering, axes, and legends; the title and page-header layout also change.

improvement.justification: The stronger baseline comparisons and controlled Contriever experiment improve support for the central contribution, while Appendix C.6 addresses v1's explicitly unexamined LM impact. BRIGHT and cross-domain experiments add useful evidence about applicability. These gains are tempered by removal of informative mechanistic ablations and explicit limitations. Moreover, Appendix C.7's new linear-in-batch-size cost claim is not reconciled with Section 3.2's pairwise attention equations. The empirical support improves overall, but these losses and analytical gaps limit the net improvement.
